archetype: A linear go-wide Vampire typal deck that kills by trigger, and the frame agrees. deck-audit reads aggro off strategic_frame.json and the deck answers to it: 29 creature copies inside the 26-32 band, threat-density 11 against a floor of 3, bracket floor 4. The precise name is a critical-mass deck whose conversion layer is enchantments rather than bodies, which is why a creature sweeper does not answer it.
verdict: The rebuild worked. The deck develops (0.921 turn-3 land drops), finds a token multiplier in 79.0% of games and a lord or anthem in 82.9%, and the interaction-breadth axis the last pass called binding now reads 5. What binds now is what that 5 is made of: Despark is the deck's only answer to a noncreature permanent, it can only target mana value 4 or greater, and the deck's own goldfish target measures it drawn in 16.8% of games. Second and smaller, the token-to-damage payoff the frame calls the conversion layer is three cards at 43.2% assembled. Everything else the audit flags UNDER is a taxonomy artefact and I am withdrawing my last pass on two of them: card-advantage counts 4 and the deck holds about a dozen draw functions, and interaction counts 12 of which roughly seven answer anything, so there are no six reclaimable slots.

axes.reading: Five classes answered, and four of them are one card deep. The audit's by_class is artifact 1, enchantment 1, graveyard 1, land 2 — and reading the cards collapses it further: Despark alone supplies artifact, enchantment and land through the catch-all pattern, and its text is 'Exile target permanent with mana value 4 or greater', so below mana value 4 the deck cannot interact with a noncreature permanent at all. The second land card is Winds of Abandon, whose only mention of land is the basic-land compensation clause. Graveyard is Cemetery Gatekeeper exiling one card once. This is the axis that binds.

axes.reading: Twelve counted, and the Short List analyst is right that the count is not an answer count. Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros carry removal:damage because they damage each opponent — they are the token plan, not the answer suite — Elspeth, Storm Slayer is a token doubler, and Cemetery Gatekeeper is graveyard exile plus a symmetric ping. What is left that answers a permanent is Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Despark, Winds of Abandon, Henrika's edict mode, Sorin's sacrifice-for-3, and Boros Charm against a planeswalker. That is at the aggro band, not six over it.

engine.declared: Eminence mints a Vampire token for every Vampire spell cast from the command zone, eight multipliers turn that token into two or four, and a conversion layer turns each entry into life loss at all three seats — with lords and Shared Animosity as the second kill and one two-card loop as the third.

The conversion layer, and the thinnest on-plan group in the deck: 43.2% assembled, 34.1% by turn six, 19.9% in an opening seven. Three copies sits under the five-copy line the corpus prices at 31% of openers. Bontu's Monument is a fourth each-opponent drain of the same family keyed on CAST rather than ENTER, which is why it does not scale with the eight multipliers and is not in this group.

lean_into.what: The conversion layer is wider than the 33.4% go-wide figure measures — ten cards across four different trigger conditions, and six checker-passed stacks between them.
lean_into.why: Goldfish declares only the three enter-triggered payoffs. Read the deck and the each-opponent conversion set is Purphoros, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call on entry; Bontu's Monument on cast; Sanctum Seeker on attack; Throne of the God-Pharaoh at your end step; Twilight Prophet on upkeep; and Vito, Sanguine Bond and Bloodthirsty Conqueror on lifegain — with Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubling every one of them during your turn. Stacks 003, 004, 006, 007 and 008 all pass on members of that set. The audit says out loud that its schema cannot express the union of several independent kills, so 33.4% is one route's rate and not the deck's. Do not cut into this set to make room; it is the part of the deck that answers the format's life-total arithmetic.

cut_candidates.why: The pilot kept Vito, Sanguine Bond and Bloodthirsty Conqueror on the grounds that they carry the surviving infinites and are Vampires that attack. That reason is true of Vito and true of the Conqueror. It is not true of Sanguine Bond: five mana, no body, no creature type, no eminence trigger, no entry for the payoffs to see, and no contribution to width — the strategic frame says this in its own words, calling it the one slot the token plan is genuinely paying for. What it buys is a second gain-half for a component measured at 4.8% assembled and 2.6% by turn six, in a deck whose curve has already drifted to modal 3 and whose ramp reads 7.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Real, and priced twice over. It orphans stack 006, a checker-passed deterministic table-kill, and takes the deck's verified-line count from six presentable to five. It halves the surviving infinite's gain-half group from two cards to one, so the 4.8% falls and the 24.0% assisted figure falls with it — the Conqueror line becomes a single named pairing that three tutors have to find. And it removes the deck's only redundancy on the one route that does not care how much life the table has. I am recommending it anyway, because a five-mana blank on the turns this deck is trying to double-spell is a worse card than a three-mana answer to the permanent that stops it, and because the frame already assigns the deck the beatdown role on the strength of that 4.8%.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json declares the enter-triggered payoffs as the conversion layer and nothing else. What does 'any each-opponent conversion payoff drawn' assemble at over the real set — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Bontu's Monument, Sanctum Seeker, Throne of the God-Pharaoh, Twilight Prophet, Vito, Sanguine Bond and Bloodthirsty Conqueror?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 33.4% go-wide figure is the only number anyone has for 'can this deck convert', and it measures one of four routes. Ten copies is 54% of openers by the corpus's own arithmetic, so the true conversion rate is plausibly double the declared one. If it is, the token-to-damage add below is an improvement rather than a repair, and the deck needs less than this diagnosis suggests. If it is not, the payoff group is the deck's real ceiling and deserves a fifth copy, not a fourth.

open_questions.question: Purphoros, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call resolving together on one eminence event through Anointed Procession and Mondrak: does one two-mana Vampire cast deal 20 to each opponent, and does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 008 verified five Purphoros triggers at 2 from four token entries plus the cast body, and stack 007 verified Bloodletter doubling a Throne end-step loss. Composing three trigger sources across one entry event, and then doubling them, is arithmetic neither stack performed. It is the difference between a token deck and a token deck that has a measured non-combat kill, and nothing about it may be presented as fact until a checker passes it.

open_questions.question: Does Edgar's attack trigger put +1/+1 counters on the team early enough for Abzan Falconer to grant flying before blockers are declared?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The frame lists it as a candidate missing line and Falconer is one of the nine cards in the 82.9% combat group. If the counters land in the declare-attackers step, the whole swarm has flying before blocks and the combat kill stops needing Cover of Darkness at all — which would settle the easiest cut in this list on evidence rather than on judgement.

open_questions.question: Does a go-wide Edgar actually lose to sweepers, or to spot removal on the lords?
open_questions.why_it_matters: deck_recon.json names this as a gap it could not close: Gregory asserts lords-eat-removal and answers it with +1/+1 counters, PapLaRiviere asserts hold-protection-for-the-wrath, and both are qualitative. This diagnosis leaves all six protection slots alone and proposes cutting Swiftfoot Boots as contested. If the lords-eat-removal read is right, the Boots stay and a board-wide instant is the wrong shape, and the prescription changes.

gaps: mean_bodies_by_turn reads 4.117 at turn six and 6.516 at turn ten, and it must NOT be read as this deck being narrow. Goldfish counts creatures cast plus tokens named on the card's own text; Edgar's eminence is a command-zone trigger on casting a Vampire spell, so every eminence token — the deck's central output — is invisible to the model, as is every doubling of it. The real width is materially higher and this repo cannot compute it.

The colour-sources figure of -11 is a floor and this diagnosis could not compute the true one. manabase.land_colors scores Bloodstained Mire, Marsh Flats, Prismatic Vista, Reflecting Pool and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth at zero black sources each; all five really do produce black, and Urborg makes every land a black source. Black's real count is materially above 25 and the 71.8% on-curve figure is correspondingly pessimistic. Settling it needs a source model that resolves fetches and land-type changers.

interaction-breadth reads 5 partly on a false positive, and the axis therefore over-reports. The 'land' class is credited to Despark (through the catch-all pattern, which adds land whenever a card answers any permanent) and to Winds of Abandon (whose only mention of land is the basic-land compensation clause). Neither answers a land. The deck's true coverage is creature deep, artifact and enchantment one card each and only at mana value 4+, graveyard one exile once, land zero.

No checker-passed stack shows this deck winning by its primary plan. Stacks 002, 003, 007 and 008 measure tokens per cast, drain per attack, drain per end step and damage per cast; 004 and 006 are the 4.8% loop. Stacks 001 and 005 and decisions/002 are already presentable: false. Cutting Sanguine Bond would take the presentable count from six to five, and nothing in this diagnosis restores it — the open question routed to resolve-stack is the cheapest way to.

`manamap pilot impact` could not produce a deck diff: 'baseline already advanced past 4 record(s) (a rebless ran before impact)'. So nothing here is grounded in a measured before/after of the ten swaps; every comparison to the previous diagnosis is a comparison of two audits, not a diff.

Findings that lean on deck_recon.json (as_of 2026-08-03) are dated meta claims and expire: the Anguished Unmaking, Command Tower and Swiftfoot Boots entries all cite an inclusion rate or a named article. The construction principles under them do not expire; the percentages do.

Ownership was not used as a ranking input. None of the three adds is in the sideboard, so all three are acquisition questions this artifact does not answer. The bench holds 30 analysable cards and one of them, Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss, is outside the colour identity and unplayable here.

Whether Corpse Knight is better than Witty Roastmaster in this shell is a judgement, not a measurement. Corpse Knight is one mana cheaper and its {W}{B} pips match a deck whose red pip share is 15.1% against a 26.4% source share; Roastmaster is red, a body of the same class, and deals damage rather than causing life loss, which matters against a Platinum Angel-style effect and nowhere else. No artifact here prices the difference.
